newsitem.title: USA: Prosecution argues for McVeigh's execution.
newsitem.headline: Prosecution argues for McVeigh's execution.

text.p: Prosecutors argued Thursday that convicted Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh should be sentenced to death, telling the jury he "believed he could take the law into his own hands and declare war on his fellow Americans."
The jury, which last week convicted McVeigh for the April 19, 1995, bombing that killed 168 people, was expected to begin deliberations on his sentence later in the day.
Delivering her closing argument in the penalty phase of McVeigh's trial, prosecutor Beth Wilkinson said McVeigh believed it was his right "to murder innocent men, women and children."
The blast at the Oklahoma City federal building injured more than 500 people in addition to the 168 killed.
"He carried out a daytime assault to insure maximum carnage," Wilkinson told the jury.

Following closing arguments by both sides, the jury will be asked to decide whether McVeigh should be executed or spend his life in prison without parole. Wilkinson told the jurors she knew that "weighing the worth of anyone's life is a gut-wrenching task."
